environment.label: Oxygen above 23% and below 30%; pressure 116.8 kPa and above
environment.note: One cell of the coverage grid (coverage.json): the oxygen bin o2_23_30 and the pressure bin p_ge116_8. The bin edges are the team's choice. No flow range and no gravity level are set. Oxygen bins: 21% with the +/-2.0 point control box (EAWG.atmospheres); 30% is the Moon Base lower bound in the challenge text and the current worst-case test oxygen (CH.moonbase; TB14639.worstcase); 36% is the highest exploration design value, 34% (EA.8.2-34, EAWG.testing), plus the same 2-point box, which is the team's extension. The challenge text gives no upper oxygen bound. Pressure bins: Edges are midpoints between pressures named in the references: 55.2 kPa (8.0 psia), 70.3 kPa (10.2 psia) and 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia) (EAWG.atmospheres, CH.moonbase). The upper edge of the 101.3 bin mirrors its lower edge. FLEX tests set to 0.7 atm are recorded at 70.2 to 72.6 kPa, so a bin around 70.3 is used instead of a strict 'at or below 70.3'. The bins are wide: the bin around 101.3 kPa spans 85.8 to below 116.8 kPa, against a control box of +/-0.2 psia in EAWG.atmospheres, and the lowest edge is built from 8.0 psia while the 8.2 psia atmosphere (EA.8.2-34) falls in the same bin.

references.text: SMACs are based on experiments at standard pressure and oxygen. Rev D applies the published ppm values across all atmospheric scenarios, including reduced-pressure exploration atmospheres, for vapor-phase compounds. 1- and 24-hour values apply to off-nominal situations such as accidental releases. The values were established for human spaceflight and are not intended to apply to other situations such as ground operations.

needs.note: Aging time is required, so this need holds the SAME tests of smoke from overheated materials. The smoke-point rows of PSI-107 (gas jet flames: the fuel flow at which the flame starts to emit soot) are a different kind of smoke condition and are not included. The SAME table has four more rows that name Kapton, Silicone Rubber, Lampwick and Dibutyl Phthalate with the words 'same conditions as 1-4' and no values; they are not read. By these words the table treats its columns, the weight loss rate among them, as conditions, while the pipeline lists the mass loss rate as the outcome of this need. The SAME-R rows (PSI-101) hold no mass loss rate and are not counted.
